intro:
Falciu — 22 June 1941

Germany has attacked along the frontier, and Romania has joined the war. Here in Bessarabia, the 150th Rifle Division faces the Prut while the Romanian forces prepare their own advance.

Form your command from the troops available for requisition, cross at Falciu and take the bridge. Establish a bridgehead from which we can meet the expected offensive. Reinforcements will be sent when they can be spared.

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

intro:
01. FALCIU 2 (7 July 1941)

The Romanian offensive is gathering across the Prut. Our bridgehead at Falciu threatens its flank, and the enemy is preparing to clear us from the far bank before advancing into Bessarabia.

Hold the bridgehead and its crossing. Reinforcements will be sent if they can be spared, but the first attacks will fall on the troops already here. Keep the supply passage open while the forward positions absorb the blow.

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

Excellent, comrade. You have stopped the Rumanian fascists! Furious fights have shown the tenacity of the Red Army in war! However the bridgehead cannot be held. As you have noticed the enemy is close to cutting us off from the rear. You have orders to pull back to our side of the Prut River and await new orders.

tactical.text:

intro:
02. KISHENEV (14 July 1941)

The German breakthrough north of us has made the Prut position untenable. Your troops have held the Romanians, but remaining here would leave the division cut off from the road east.

Withdraw through Kishenev towards Odessa. Kishenev controls the last road out of Bessarabia still in our hands; secure it before the pursuing columns reach the junction. Keep the division together through the retreat.

intro:
Odessa — 13 August 1941

Romanian forces have reached Odessa while the German advance has cut our land routes east. The port is still supplied by the Black Sea Fleet, but everything the garrison needs must now come by sea from the Crimea.

Hold the approaches and keep your formations alive while the fleet sustains the defence. Fall back into stronger positions when necessary, with the guns covering the movement. Headquarters needs time and an army that can be brought out when the order comes.

Campaign note: survive the full 20 turns. The scripted defeat then continues the campaign; there is no winning grade here.

intro:
04. PEREKOP (25 September 1941)

Odessa is still holding, but German forces have reached the narrow entrance to the Crimea. Their attack has nearly carried the Perekop isthmus, and reserves can follow through any gap left open there.

Counterattack and recover the Perekop positions before the enemy can widen the passage. The roads beyond lead into the peninsula and towards Sevastopol. Stop the advance while its strength is still confined to this narrow front.

You will be drawn back from the front for rest and possible refitting.

intro:
05. ROSTOV 1941 (25 November 1941)

Rostov has fallen to German mobile formations. The city is the gateway to the Caucasus, but the speed of the enemy advance has left a salient projecting into our line. Winter has reached the steppe, and headquarters has ordered a counterattack.

Retake Rostov and threaten the roads behind its garrison. Force the German armour to defend the city while our neighbouring formations press its flanks. The crossing must be back in our hands before the enemy can use it to carry the offensive south.

BRILLIANT VICTORY

Excellent comrade!!! This is one of first big victories of this war. You have driven some elite forces of the fascists armies out of Rostov and saved the Caucasus from an attack! However many of the almost entrapped Germans managed to retreat and built up a defensive winter line at the Mius River, still tens of kilometers west of Rostov!

06. KERCH (26 December 1941)

Sevastopol is still holding, but the rest of the Crimea is in German and Romanian hands. A landing at the eastern end of the peninsula will threaten the rear of the forces attacking the fortress.

Bring your troops across from Taman and land around Kerch. Take the town and join the separate landing groups before the coastal defenders can gather for a counterattack. The army needs a foothold large enough to receive the guns and supplies coming behind you.

The enemy was quick enough to retreat and build a new defensive line, but we are in possession of the Kerch peninsula from Kerch to Feodisya and have drained away enemy forces that could otherwise attack Sevastopol.

The landing at Kerch is one part of our attempt to draw pressure away from Sevastopol. Your force will come ashore farther west, at Feodosiya, threatening the connection between the Kerch peninsula and the rest of the Crimea.

Take Feodosiya and secure the landing approaches. The German coastal troops are spread out, but they can concentrate quickly once our direction is clear. Open the port and bring the landing groups together before that response arrives.

The Crimean landings — 15 December 1941

Sevastopol is under pressure. Landings in the eastern Crimea will threaten the enemy's rear and draw forces away from the siege. Your command can join the attack at Kerch or the landing farther west at Feodosiya.

Take the first selection position for Kerch, or the second for Feodosiya. The army's subsequent orders will bring both routes back into the same campaign.

intro:
Sevastopol — 6 June 1942

The next assault on Sevastopol is beginning. Months of bombardment and repeated attacks have worn down the garrison, and supplies are increasingly difficult to bring across the Black Sea. The fleet is carrying your troops in to reinforce the defence.

Hold for fifteen days while headquarters decides the next step. Keep the approaches covered, shorten exposed parts of the line when necessary and preserve the formations that can still fight. We have few replacements to send into the fortress.

intro:
10. NOVOROSSIYSK 1 (20 September 1942)

The German summer offensive has reached the Caucasus. Rostov and the Maikop oilfields are lost, and the enemy has entered Novorossiysk. The coastal road beyond it leads towards the ports still supplying our forces along the Black Sea.

Stop the southward advance and recover the hill positions covering the road. We cannot yet retake the whole port. Hold the line that prevents the enemy from carrying its success farther down the coast.

11. SUCHUMI (28 September 1942)

The coastal advance has been checked, but German mountain troops are coming through the Caucasus towards Suchumi. They threaten to reach the Black Sea behind the front and cut its only coastal supply road.

Hold the port and the positions covering the mountain approaches. Keep the coastal road open to the troops near Novorossiysk. The enemy must be stopped as he emerges from the passes, before his columns can spread along the shore.

intro:
12. ORDZHONIKIDZE 1 (1 November 1942)

The First Panzer Army is advancing across the Terek towards the routes serving Grozny and Baku. After a heavy bombardment, its troops are closing on Ordzhonikidze, a junction we cannot afford to lose.

Bring one group into the town from the eastern assembly area while the force to the north strikes the German flank. The garrison must hold while that counterattack develops. Snow complicates supply off the roads; keep the ammunition columns within reach of the guns.

13. ORDZHONIKIDZE 2 (8 November 1942)

Ordzhonikidze has held, and the attack on the German flank has cut the supply route behind their forward troops. Enemy reinforcements are now coming to reopen it, while the trapped formations prepare to break out.

Keep the two forces apart, defeat the encircled group and carry the advance west. Hold the road junctions against the relief attack. The town will be threatened again if the Germans restore their connection before we clear the pocket.

The encirclement at Stalingrad has changed the position in the Caucasus. German forces are withdrawing, with roads west towards Novorossiysk and Taman and another route north-west through Rostov.

Retake Maikop and its oilfields, then advance to the Kuban. Threaten the western roads so the retreating columns must turn towards the forces approaching from the Don. The provisional airstrip can service aircraft already here, but cannot receive newly deployed squadrons.

We are back at the approaches to Rostov. German columns are still coming out of the Caucasus, and the Don crossings offer their mobile formations a route into Ukraine.

Land with the naval infantry south of the city and join the force attacking along the coast. Cruisers and destroyers will support the landing. Unite the two attacks before the defenders can contain the beachhead and turn back to the coastal front.

The Kuban defences have resisted a month of attacks. German and Romanian troops still hold Novorossiysk and the approaches to Krymskaya; now they are counterattacking our southern bridgehead.

Strike at Krymskaya to draw reserves away from that threatened foothold and break the centre of the enemy line. More of our forces are being committed, but the Germans also have reserves close enough to answer a breakthrough. Keep the attack moving beyond the first positions.

Novorossiysk has fallen, and the retreating enemy is moving towards Taman. Across the strait lies the Crimea, where troops evacuated from this bridgehead can form another defensive line.

Other forces will start attacks in Byelorussia and the Baltics.

21. SEVASTOPOL 1944 (7 May 1944)

The German and Romanian troops driven back through the Crimea have gathered at Sevastopol. The fortress we once defended is now the last major base from which they can hold the peninsula or evacuate it.

Take the city before the garrison can get away by sea. The march has stretched our supplies, and some of the infantry is still coming forward. Keep the roads clear for those formations while the leading troops force the outer defences.

22. JASSY (15 June 1944)

Our bridgehead across the Prut near Jassy gives the army a starting point for the next offensive into Romania. German and Romanian forces are gathering to destroy it while its garrison is short of men and supplies.

Hold the far bank. You may shorten the perimeter where necessary, but keep a connected position and the crossings supplying it. Watch for German armour massing against a narrow part of the line.

The offensive has broken through from the Prut bridgeheads. Enemy formations are withdrawing between our advancing groups, and a junction near Falciu could close their route out.

Drive south along the western bank to meet the forces crossing from the Kishenev direction. Take Falciu and secure the crossings between the two columns. We fought to hold a bridge here in 1941; now the enemy needs it to get away.

Romania has changed sides, and Romanian formations are now fighting the Germans. German troops are withdrawing through the countryside while others try to hold positions around Bucharest. Your force is closest to the capital.

25. RUSE (8 September 1944)

War has been declared on Bulgaria, and our force is to cross the Danube. The Bulgarian army has been ordered not to resist, but some troops may not have received those orders and German forces remain in the country.

Secure the crossings at Ruse and Turlukai and move onto the inland junctions. Establish contact before opening fire where troops offer no resistance. Keep the columns ready to deal with armed opposition without turning every uncertain encounter into a battle.

26. SOFIA (12 September 1944)

Our advance has met little resistance, but armed forces loyal to the old government are reported on the approaches to Sofia. Partisan groups in the area can help us reach the capital and secure it.

Take Sofia and the positions covering its roads. Keep contact with the local forces as the columns advance; the situation is changing quickly, and reports about the strength and intentions of the remaining garrisons are incomplete.
